subject: Packaging advice — microbundle vs metered credits
messages:
From: Erin Cole <erin.cole@novusai.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@novusai.com
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging question: microbundles vs metered credits

Hi David,

Quick one — we're evaluating Redwood for two different workloads: a high-throughput inference path for our inference-heavy pipelines and a lower-volume R&D sandbox used by data scientists. Finance is pushing for predictable committed pricing, but engineering likes the flexibility of metered credits (pay-for-usage).

Can you send a short write-up of where Redwood recommends microbundles (small fixed bundles for predictable teams) vs. credit-based metering? Specifics we care about: upgrade/downgrade friction, how feature entitlements map to bundles, and what discount tiers look like at 6/12/24 month commitments.

We have an internal sizing file attached if that helps.

Thanks —
Erin Cole
Head of Platform, Novus AI
(attachment: Novus_sizing_report.csv, 42 KB)
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging question: microbundles vs metered credits

Thanks Erin — great context. High level guidance below and I attached a concise feature matrix for Novus-specific mapping.

Option A — Microbundles (recommended for predictable teams):
- Fixed monthly token/throughput allocation per bundle.
- Clear feature entitlements (priority routing, KV cache retention tiers, model variant pins).
- Simple upgrade path: mid-cycle prorated top-up or next-cycle tier swap; downgrade locks until end of term unless you accept a 30% step-down fee.
- Best when usage variance < 30% month-over-month.

Option B — Metered credits (recommended for bursty/R&D workloads):
- Pay-per-token credits consumed; no long-term seat/throughput guarantees unless you add committed base credits.
- Flexible scaling, immediate consumption-based billing.
- Lower friction to start but costs can spike without KV caching and batching tuned.

Discount guidance (ballpark):
- 6mo commit: 8–12% on list for bundle commitments >= 200M tokens/month equivalent.
- 12mo commit: 12–18% for higher commits and multi-region SLAs.
- 24mo: 18–25% with additional operational credits (free pilot seats, rollout support).

Hybrid suggestion for Novus: start with a 3–6 month pilot on metered credits for R&D + a microbundle for core inference (6mo) to get predictable unit economics. After pilot, convert R&D to committed bundle if usage stabilizes and offer a conversion credit.

Attached: feature_matrix.xlsx (mapping of features to bundle tiers) and a sample SOW.

Next step — if you can share typical monthly token ranges for core inference vs. R&D (ballpark is fine), I can propose 2 priced options (pilot+annual conversion) and an estimated discount schedule.

Best,
David Kim
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: FW: Packaging question: microbundles vs metered credits

Kimberly / Priyom — looping you in. Novus (Erin Cole) sent usage buckets and is asking for: onboarding/rollout credits on a 12mo commit, flexibility on downgrade fees, and clear conversion credit terms.

My suggested offer to keep the deal moving:
- 12mo committed core bundle at 350M tokens/month baseline with 18% list discount.
- Conversion credit: 1.5x of the pilot-months' spend applied once they convert R&D to a committed bundle within 90 days of pilot end (cap at $25k).
- Onboarding: $15k operational credit (applied to first invoice) + two free migration days from our solutions team.
- Downgrade protection: allow a single mid-term step-down with 10% administrative fee (instead of 30%) if they notify 30 days prior and remain above 60% baseline after step-down.

Can we approve 18% discount + the $15k onboarding credit? If not, what's the max on discount we can offer without AE manager signoff?

Thanks —
David
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: FW: Packaging question: microbundles vs metered credits

David — thanks for the draft. Approve the $15k onboarding credit and one free migration day (we'll bill second day at discounted rate if used).

Discount: approve up to 15% standard, but 18% requires AM/AE manager approval. If Novus is willing to sign a 12mo + auto-renew clause and provide a short-term banked commit (quarterly reserve), we can stretch to 18% and include the conversion credit cap.

Downgrade fee: approve the reduced 10% admin fee as a concession for strategic account. Make sure legal stamps the exact step-down language (30-day notice, floor of 60% baseline).

Priyom — please prepare a clean redline for SOW_NovusAI_v1.docx with the above concessions and a clause for pilot-to-commit conversion credits.

—Kimberly

Erin — thanks for the details. Based on internal approval, here is a concrete proposal for Novus AI: 

Offer (summary):
1) Pilot + Convert path (recommended):
  - 3 month metered pilot for R&D (no upfront commit). During the pilot we provide: 1) onboarding credit $15k applied to first invoice, 2) two free migration days (second day billed at discounted rate if used).
  - If Novus converts R&D to a 12-month committed microbundle within 90 days of pilot completion, we will apply a conversion credit equal to 1.5x the pilot monthly spend (capped at $25,000).

2) Core inference bundle (12mo):
  - Baseline: 350M tokens/month committed for 12 months.
  - Discount: 18% off list conditional on signing 12mo with auto-renew and quarterly banked commit (standard commercial terms attached).
  - Downgrade: single permitted mid-term step-down with 10% admin fee, 30-day notice, floor at 60% of original baseline.

Attachments: SOW_NovusAI_v1.docx (redline forthcoming per our legal), feature_matrix.xlsx, Novus_sizing_report.csv.

Next steps:
- I can send a DocuSign for the 12mo core bundle and SOW addendum if this aligns. Procurement, let me know if the auto-renew + quarterly banked commit is acceptable; if not we can present a counter (15% discount floor).

Happy to hop on a 30-min call tomorrow to walk the team through the conversion mechanics and billing cadence.

Best,
David Kim
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
